_comment: Asset inventory. This is the business context a scanner cannot supply.
A CVSS 10 on an isolated lab host and a CVSS 6 on an internet-facing
production server are not the same risk, and no amount of vulnerability
data will tell you which is which. That judgement comes from here.
In an enterprise this would be drawn from a CMDB. Stage 5 replaces this
The weights below are the narrowed second configuration. The first used
0.6-1.5 and 0.7-1.3, giving a 3.7x spread between the two assets, which
let asset context overwhelm exploit evidence: findings with no EPSS data
ranked above the highest-scoring vulnerability in the dataset. Narrowing
to a 1.65x spread corrected the ordering. See docs/stage4-risk-scoring.md.

192.168.32.128.name: metasploitable
192.168.32.128.description: Deliberately vulnerable host, isolated lab network

_weighting_comment: How the attributes above convert to a multiplier.
Criticality and exposure are deliberately kept separate. A critical
system on an isolated network and an unimportant one on the public
internet are different problems, and collapsing them into one number
loses the distinction that decides which gets fixed first.
